summary.prose: Add a Settings-discoverable connection manager to the standalone VS Code extension and upgrade the IDE fork’s Data Sources editor to the same behavior. Users explicitly choose a registered repository and Saved or Temporary scope, filter by lifetime, edit safe driver-specific fields, test drafts, and Delete or Discard with truthful recovery states. Workbench-owned temporary connections survive closing the manager; incomplete backend release evidence continues to block production admission.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a daemon-owned application service over the existing repository JSON registry and driver implementations. Separate saved commit, runtime activation and client refresh; use immutable credential generations and atomic JSON replacement rather than pretending the filesystem and keychain share a transaction. Temporary configurations remain in daemon memory under a workbench lease. All descriptions below are proposed architecture, not assertions of current implementation.

ownedContracts.name: Manager state and scope filter
ownedContracts.purpose: Preserve the PRD interaction across the two client implementations.
ownedContracts.interfaceSketch: type ScopeFilter = 'all'|'saved'|'temporary'; type ConnectionListState = 'loading'|'ready'|'empty-registry'|'empty-filter'|'read-error'|'offline'|'no-repository'|'upgrade-required'; interface ConnectionManagerState { repoRoot?: string | undefined; filter: ScopeFilter; listState: ConnectionListState; draftRevision: number; dirty: boolean; mutationOperationId?: string | undefined; refreshError?: string | undefined }

consumedContracts.name: Connection management protocol and driver descriptors
consumedContracts.purpose: One safe wire contract and compatibility boundary for all consumers.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: type ConnectionScope = 'saved' | 'temporary'; interface ConnectionKey { repoRoot: string; scope: ConnectionScope; id: string } interface SafeConnection { key: ConnectionKey; revision: string; kind: string; family: 'rdbms'|'kv'|'file'; label?: string | undefined; publicConfig: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; declaredFamily?: string | undefined; registeredFamily?: string | undefined; effectiveFamily: string; compatibilityWarning?: string | undefined; credentialPresence: Readonly<Record<string, boolean>> } type CredentialPatch = { action: 'keep' } | { action: 'replace'; value: string } | { action: 'clear' }; interface DriverDescriptor { kind: string; family: 'rdbms'|'kv'|'file'; publicInputSchema: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; secretSlots: readonly string[] } interface ManagementCapabilities { version: 2; daemonEpoch: string; features: readonly string[]; receiptRetentionDays: 30 }

consumedContracts.name: Revision-checked mutation and recovery outcomes
consumedContracts.purpose: Make persistence and retries truthful across registry and credential boundaries.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: interface OperationTicket { operationId: string; lookupRoot: string; scope: ConnectionScope; connectionId: string; mode: "create"|"update"|"remove"; issuedAt: string; expiresAt: string; signature: string } interface OperationStatusRequest { ticket: OperationTicket } interface MutationRequest { ticket: OperationTicket; operationId: string; key: ConnectionKey; mode: 'create'|'update'|'remove'; expectedRevision?: string | undefined; publicPatch?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined; credentials?: Readonly<Record<string, CredentialPatch>> | undefined } type ManagementErrorCode = 'invalid-input'|'duplicate-id'|'conflict'|'not-found'|'busy'|'registry-unreadable'|'secret-unavailable'|'recovery-required'|'session-expired'|'upgrade-required'|'operation-mismatch'|'reconciliation-required'; interface CommittedOutcome { operationId: string; revision: string; registration: 'persisted'|'session-added'|'removed'; activation: 'active'|'pending'|'failed'|'not-applicable'; credentialCleanup: 'complete'|'pending' } type MutationOutcome = { status: 'committed'; value: CommittedOutcome } | { status: 'rejected'; code: ManagementErrorCode; message: string }; type OperationStatus = { status:'committed'; value:CommittedOutcome } | { status:'pending'|'not-seen'|'reconciliation-required' }; interface ActivationRetry { key: ConnectionKey; committedRevision: string }

consumedContracts.name: Validated connection access context and driver leases
consumedContracts.purpose: A foundational extension point for session isolation and busy-use correctness across dependency branches.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: interface ConnectionAccessContext { lookupRoot: string; managementRepoRoot?: string | undefined; daemonEpoch: string; sessionHandle?: string | undefined } interface ConnectionLease { key: ConnectionKey; revision: string; release(): Promise<void> } interface ConnectionResolver { list(context: ConnectionAccessContext): Promise<readonly SafeConnection[]>; lease(context: ConnectionAccessContext, id: string): Promise<ConnectionLease> } interface ManagementRequestContext { connectionIdentity: string; access: ConnectionAccessContext }

consumedContracts.name: Transient draft test contract
consumedContracts.purpose: Test the same draft as Save with bounded lifetime and stale-result identity.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: interface DraftTestRequest { requestId: string; draftRevision: number; key: ConnectionKey; expectedRevision?: string | undefined; publicPatch: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; credentials: Readonly<Record<string, CredentialPatch>> } interface DraftTestResult { requestId: string; draftRevision: number; repoRoot: string; daemonEpoch: string; status: 'reachable'|'failed'|'timeout'|'canceled'; tookMs: number; safeMessage?: string | undefined } interface TestCancellation { requestId: string }

consumedContracts.name: Workbench session registration and ephemeral overlay
consumedContracts.purpose: Memory-only temporary state independent from panels and chat sessions.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: interface OpenConnectionSessionResult { sessionHandle: string; capability: string; daemonEpoch: string; heartbeatMs: 30000; leaseMs: 90000 } interface SessionResume { sessionHandle: string; capability: string; daemonEpoch: string } interface TemporaryConnectionStore { register(context: ConnectionAccessContext, request: MutationRequest): Promise<MutationOutcome>; end(sessionHandle: string): Promise<void> }

consumedContracts.name: Safe removal and cleanup presentation
consumedContracts.purpose: Treat saved Delete and temporary Discard consistently without touching source data.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: interface RemoveConnectionRequest { ticket: OperationTicket; operationId: string; key: ConnectionKey; expectedRevision: string } interface RemovalState { key: ConnectionKey; operationId: string; state: 'confirming'|'removing'|'busy'|'conflict'|'unknown'|'removed-cleanup-pending'|'removed'; safeMessage?: string | undefined }

boundary.internal: Settings contributions and shared command routing, themed editor/forms, filters, dirty guards, stale-test suppression and truthful feedback in extension and external IDE. HLD has inspected the external pane, actions, service, mirrored types and Settings registrations; S005 implements the recorded plan and validates its mirrored contract before integration acceptance.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Safe saved-config read/patch, canonical repo validation, driver profiles, registry metadata/receipts and crash recovery, immutable secret generation staging, compatibility adapters and lease accounting foundation. Does not own temporary storage or rich manager layout. Preserve saved-only scope-local lookup and legacy pinned-family values; signed operation tickets make expiry/replay decidable after receipt pruning. Own the shared memory-only conversion/probe driver foundation, converter-cache policy/identity changes and private DuckDB lifecycle (sc8), completed before the S002/S003 branches.
Transient process probe transport, deadline/cancellation and sanitization. Uses foundational context slots without depending on s3’s session implementation.

Session open/resume/heartbeat/end, memory-only temporary overlays and receipts, trusted execution-context propagation through analyzer/tool/MCP call paths, expiry and saved/temporary collision rules. Bind the S001-owned sc8 file execution policy to session identity and expiry; S001 owns conversion, cache-policy isolation and private DuckDB lifecycle. Every native/converted kind uses that foundation rather than a branch-local converter.
Removal coordination for both scopes, busy/revision enforcement, confirmation state, postcommit credential cleanup retry and operation-status recovery. Never invokes source data deletion.

nonFunctional.performance: Draft tests have a 10-second parent-enforced deadline, with forced child reap if graceful termination fails. Workbench heartbeat is 30 seconds and expiry 90 seconds after last valid heartbeat. Mutations serialize per repo; list/filter work does not perform driver probes. LLD load tests must verify no leaked children, leases or session entries after cancellation/expiry.
nonFunctional.security: Daemon owns every saved/temporary config and credential decision; client labels/PIDs are not authorization. Registered-root eligibility gates management and temporary operations; saved-only analysis preserves canonical scope-local lookup without gaining mutation rights. Safe read responses return a profile allowlist and presence booleans only. Secrets, capabilities and full requests never enter logs, receipts, prompts, artifacts, telemetry or checkpoints. Temporary inputs never reach disk or keychain. A test worker receives config via private IPC and may not emit raw driver errors. Temporary file conversion, query spill and metadata/logging are part of the no-persistence boundary, including test workers.
nonFunctional.observability: Use getLogger with operation ID, safe code, repo ID, scope, revision and phase only; timing and counters for commit, activation, recovery, timeout, busy refusal and session expiry. No raw exceptions or endpoint/options. Operation status exposes committed truth even when response delivery or activation failed. Recovery-required and cleanup-pending are visible and actionable.
nonFunctional.durability: Saved JSON remains authoritative. Same-directory atomic rename/fsync commits registry, revisions and receipts together; immutable keychain generations preserve previous effective credentials until commit. Recover preparation records before enabling mutation. Issue signed 30-day operation tickets; preserve receipts through ticket expiry and pending cleanup, and distinguish expired-unreceipted from valid-not-seen after restart. Temporary state and receipts expire on explicit session end, 90-second lease loss or daemon epoch change.

dataModelChanges.details: Proposed pure core in src/shared/connection-manager/{model,controller,wire}.ts (new files, no daemon/storage/provider imports). Mirror only this reviewed pure module closure into IDE common/connectionManagement via deterministic sync manifest with source/destination hashes and divergence refusal; no separate package/runtime dependency. Both renderers consume the same reducer/events/effect descriptors; injected adapters execute effects. One workbench controller owns 0..many per-root manager views; each view has 0..1selected key, 0..1draft and monotonically increasing view generation. UI selection never grants backend authority. Keep selected repo/filter in workbench memory; reject stale list/read responses on root+view-generation+epoch mismatch. Do not persist temporary state in webview getState/setState, memento, Settings, logs or telemetry. Persistence of non-sensitive preferences is unnecessary for this scope. The extension manager owns proposed vscode-plugin/src/connections/{types,host,wiring,renderer}.ts modules. Existing vscode-plugin/src/panels/types.ts remains unchanged: it is a reference for injection patterns only, not a connection-state extension point.

Settings keyword group 'insrc connections' exposes a command link Manage Connections; it is discovery text, not a writable URL/options/scope setting. Standalone extension adds insrc.openDataSources and legacy add/edit/remove/test aliases only where absent, all to one manager route. Existing IDE command/editor IDs retained. No-repository shows register guidance; multiple registered workspace roots require explicit selection, none inferred. A retained selected root wins over active editor; if registration is removed, invalidate selection. Successful zero rows => empty-registry; nonempty total but zero filtered => empty-filter; failed read/offline/upgrade states distinct, retry only re-reads. Preserve last-good rows as visibly stale non-actionable context on error, never count as authoritative. All/Saved/Temporary counts computed before filter for selected root; search then filter matching count is explicit. Add reveals committed row by switching to matching scope or All and selecting exact new key/revision; does not fake a successful refresh.

Wire unchanged. Add separate v2 methods and result decoders to IDE service/types; preserve legacy list/save/test/remove signatures for unrelated callers, but v2 manager never calls swallowed-error list or legacy upsert/delete. Validate capabilities, descriptors, lists, safe read, signed-ticket target, mutation/status/test/removal replies as exact discriminated structures with size/depth bounds. Validate descriptors with supported schema subset; unknown required input/schema kind => driver unavailable/read-only with safe guidance, never infer endpoint format or accept arbitrary options. Every daemon descriptor offered with unsupported/read-only explanation if not editable. Fixed edit ID/kind/scope/family; pinned legacy family and unknown private fields stay server-side. Credential Keep default on existing slots, Replace masked blank new value, Clear explicit confirmation; do not round-trip presence booleans as secret values.

Wire unchanged. Host holds effective UI draft only in memory and increments draftRevision on every field/credential edit. Test and Save share one draft serializer; Test is optional, never saves, emits requestId/revision/key/expectedRevision/publicPatch/credential intent. Only one in-flight probe per transport; cancellation on edit, root/scope/selection switch and close. Display result only when requestId,draftRevision,repoRoot,epoch plus locally captured full key/view-generation all match. Ignore late results and retain safe elapsed duration. Preserve the source controller till daemon drain completes even if panel closes; timeout/cancel response is not proof of cleanup. Raw SDK/transport exceptions replaced with fixed local messages.

No wire/persistent-schema change. Each manager view has at most one active mutation and one memory-only immutable attempted request (including credential intent), paired with signed ticket. Freeze exact draft before ticket/mutate; disable duplicate submit. Lost delivery => unknown, retain draft and same operation, never reset to editable form and create a new ID. Status pending continues bounded/backoff polling with explicit retry; not-seen permits only identical same-ticket replay after explicit action; expired/unreceipted => reconciliation-required, no replay. Saved disconnect/reconnect may reconcile same ticket on an unclaimed Saved lane; temporary reconnect resumes only matching live owner/epoch and current root delegation. Committed response clears sensitive draft, reports saved/session-added independently from activation and refresh; retry activation by committed revision or list refresh only, never repeat mutation. Closing dirty draft uses Discard/Cancel; unknown mutation close may hide the view but workbench retains its reconciliation record and reopens it before new target mutation. No disk recovery store; after workbench loss Saved requires authoritative reload/status only when ticket still in memory, otherwise describe uncertain last operation without inventing outcome.

Consume current independent credentialCleanup/resourceCleanup projection, not older HLD illustrative simplification. Exact selection confirmation shows repository+scope+ID and source-data guarantee. Busy/conflict keep row, selection and draft; conflict reload requires reconfirm fresh revision. Unknown never inferred removed from absent list row. Committed removed-cleanup-pending removes usable registration from authoritative rows but retains a separate operation status card with both cleanup phases; retry sends only {ticket}. Cannot close a recreated generation. Cancel uses zero ticket/mutation effects. S00420consumer snapshots reused for state copy; actual rendering/keyboard evidence still required in both clients.

One workbench lifetime owns one memory-only session and dedicated multiplexed control socket, initially opened with selected registered root. Heartbeat every30s while workbench live; end on actual disposal, not manager close/root switch. Extend existing thin src/shared/ipc-client.ts socket code with persistent request-ID multiplexing and sanitized disconnect outcome, preserving one-shot exports unchanged; no independent socket implementation in extension. Control lane carries only session open/resume/delegate/heartbeat/end plus permitted metadata; per-root workbench-ui delegated data sockets carry temporary management and scoped analysis/tool/probe calls. Saved actions use separate unclaimed sockets. Root switching delegates existing owner to new registered root, never creates a new owner or discards previous overlay. Same-root data channels may carry concurrent bound requests but no raw capabilities reach renderer. On disconnect stop dependent effects, resume old in-memory owner within90s and same epoch then re-delegate/attach current generation; expired/new epoch clears temporary UI/attempt records, cancels drafts/tests, displays lifetime loss, no silent recreation. Temporary copy shown before Add: survives panelclose/root switch; ends on workbench end,90s lease loss or daemonrestart. No guessed heartbeat extends a daemon deadline.

Current IDE generic daemon service funnels renderer RPCs through a global main-process socket, so it cannot host workbench-bound sc5 claims. S005 client integration adds a window-scoped management channel in /Users/subhagho/work/projects/insors/insrc-ide/src/vs/code/electron-main/app.ts and /Users/subhagho/work/projects/insors/insrc-ide/src/vs/platform/insrc/electron-main/insrcDaemonMainService.ts, using trusted Electron IPC caller/window identity from server context, never JSON windowId or labels. Main owns 1control+0..many root-data sockets per trusted window and a separate Saved lane; exact allowlisted management/session/scoped execution methods, request IDs and result events routed only to owner. Browser/electron-sandbox daemonServiceImpl exposes typed intent API with no capability serialization to browser/editor state; lifecycle disposal tied to window lifecycle. Existing global generic channel remains unclaimed Saved/legacy traffic. Two renderer pending RPC maps cannot consume each other's reply IDs; collision tests mandatory. This is client transport adaptation of sc5, not new daemon authorization. If trusted caller identity cannot be established at build, block external integration and raise amendment/question; never use payload identity. External edits require tracked commits and authorized filesystem access before execution.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Pure manager model, counts, mutually distinct list states, retained repo, explicit scope, dirty navigation, generation-bound tests and truthful effects; independent host rendering.
Strict capabilities/descriptors/safe reads and feature-by-feature fail-closed admission; no new wire contract.
Consume signed operation/status and activation semantics unchanged; immutable same-ticket retry, no persistence inference from transport delivery.
Client conveys only trusted scoped session lane; daemon owns leases, authority and global busy enforcement.
Draft-test serializer/cancel/result identity consumed unchanged; true drain is daemon owned.
Workbench memory-only control owner, per-root delegated UI/data sockets, explicit resume/end and90s lifetime; no panel/chat session lifetime.
Consume S004 confirmation/state/ticket-only cleanup and independent phases; never delete source or select cleanup by current ID.
Consume unsupported/resource-limit messages without local conversion/cache/spill fallback; file runtime remains daemon-owned.

errorCases.detection: Capabilities decoder rejects shape/version/epoch or required feature set is missing; unknown-method replies are classified as upgrade-required.
errorCases.response: Show upgrade-required and disable affected add/edit/test/remove controls, with metadata readable only if that feature is advertised. No legacy mutation fallback and no synthetic positive gate evidence shipped.
errorCases.userImpact: Can see explicit compatibility guidance rather than unsafe forms.

errorCases.detection: Rejected transport call or strict bounded decoder/schema-subset validation fails before render/use.
errorCases.response: read-error/offline as appropriate; preserve last-good view marked stale, disable mutations; do not show zero counts, empty registry or invent fields. Fixed safe error text.
errorCases.userImpact: Draft stays in memory; Retry reads only.

errorCases.scenario: Mutation reply lost or timed out after possible write
errorCases.detection: Transport reports written-but-unanswered/disconnected, RPC timeout or malformed outcome on an attempted operation.
errorCases.response: Unknown state freezes exact request+ticket and blocks new mutation for target; status and identical same-ticket replay only under sc2 rules. Reconnect Saved separately; never send changed payload or fresh ticket.
errorCases.userImpact: No duplicate create/delete or false success; explicit reconciliation action.

errorCases.scenario: Committed save but activation or authoritative refresh failed
errorCases.detection: Validated committed outcome plus failed activation phase/list call.
errorCases.response: Show Saved/Added for this session separately from activation/refresh failures; retry failed effect only. Clear credential replacements after known commit. Do not reset truth to unsaved.
errorCases.userImpact: User sees committed data with actionable partial success.

errorCases.detection: Validated busy/conflict rejection or exact expectedRevision differs after reload.
errorCases.response: Keep row/draft and safe explanation. Busy retry after work ends; stale must refresh/read and reconfirm revision. Independent cleanup pending keeps operation card and sends ticket-only retry.
errorCases.userImpact: No source-data deletion, row loss or old retry closing new handle.

errorCases.detection: session-expired response, failed same-epoch resume or capabilities epoch differs; local timer never claims authoritative renewal.
errorCases.response: Revoke lane/view generation; cancel tests, clear temporary inputs/attempt records and show expired registration guidance. Require new explicit session/add; preserve Saved operations for separate reconciliation.
errorCases.userImpact: Expired temporary rows unavailable; no silent persistence/recreation.

errorCases.detection: Main-process IPC context owner differs, unknown lane, wrong root/generation or forbidden method; IDs correlated within owner lane.
errorCases.response: Refuse before socket send/lookup, route fixed failure only to caller. No JSON window ID authorization, no global broadcast of sensitive results or capabilities.

errorCases.scenario: Late test/list reply after editing or navigation
errorCases.response: Ignore for visible state, cancel prior work and retain drain ownership. Do not paint success on another draft.

errorCases.scenario: External checkout drift or missing trusted caller integration
errorCases.detection: Pinned source/commit/sync manifest check fails or IPC ownership test cannot bind to trusted Electron identity.
errorCases.response: Stop only cross-repo integration task; report explicit dependency/amendment instead of guessing caller identity or stamping both-client acceptance.
errorCases.userImpact: Release remains gated; approved backend work unaffected.

edgeCases.expected: Different empty-registry and empty-filter copy; All/Saved/Temporary counts use authoritative selected-root snapshot.

edgeCases.input: Add Temporary while Saved filter selected
edgeCases.expected: Scope default is Saved unless explicitly chosen; successful temporary add reveals new row by scope/All adjustment after actual refresh. Show lifecycle copy before adding.

edgeCases.input: Dirty navigation, root/filter/row/scope change, removal or panelclose
edgeCases.expected: Discard/Cancel before leaving dirty form; Discard means throw away unsaved draft only, not temporary registration. Scope fixed when editing. Unknown operations retained at workbench level on hide; unresolved targets reopen reconciliation before another mutation.

edgeCases.input: Read-only legacy pinned family or unknown private fields
edgeCases.expected: Safe read-only guidance and confirmation removal remain if advertised; no JSON editor to bypass descriptor constraints or silent family normalization.

edgeCases.expected: Same workbench owner retains overlays A andB; other window independent session/control/data sockets. No parent shared socket capability. No end on panelclose.
Actionable safe refusal; do not perform client conversion or write cache/source/sidecars. Test failure does not persist draft.

VSCode tokens, programmatic labels, focus-visible, logical navigation, focus restored to initiating row/toolbar after modal; status/error live region. Password inputs masked without accidental reveal from presence booleans.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Daemon remains authority for configs, credentials, atomic operation receipts and revision leases; client core imports only pure shared modules. Grounded by s1 symbol/data-model bundles.
Existing thin shared IPC one-shot public API remains compatible; persistent workbench lane extends the same boundary, not a new backend/storage path. Grounded by s1 source supplement.
Existing IDE editor identity and action IDs preserved; v2 uses a separate typed service surface instead of changing legacy array projections. Grounded by s1 external source supplement.
S004 source-preservation, exact ticket/revision retry and independent cleanup phases remain unchanged. Grounded by s1 removal usage and handoff.
Production release gate stays disabled until genuine both-client and backend prerequisites are verified; no test fixture is product acceptance.

testStrategy.testFramework: Extend existing node:test + node:assert/strict injectable extension cores and fake webview/command ports, as found by s1 source/test inspection; Node22+tsx for backend/shared and extension tests. IDE uses its existing workbench browser test runner and actual Electron IPC integration harness; discover exact invocation from that checkout before build. Include explicit extension test paths: backend src/** glob alone excludes vscode-plugin. No fabricated browser/native acceptance.

migration.stateBefore: S1 backend analyzer locates v2types/session/removal helpers; source supplement confirms extension has injectable panels/commands but no current connection manager. IDE still uses legacy Data Sources input/pane, generic globally shared main socket and service list errors→[]. migration.stateAfter: Both VSCode clients have Settings/palette/editor routing into common sc7 state semantics, safe descriptor forms, explicit registered root and scope, full-key counts, memory-only workbench session transport, generation-safe Test, signed same-operation recovery and S004 removal presentation. Separate privileged per-window transport verified; backend schemas, credentials/registry ownership and release requirements unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Freeze both checkout commits and current integration files; pin generated consumer module closure and verify uncommitted source drift. Track external edits under this S005 ledger and obtain filesystem access through normal escalation before writes. No external edits during design.

Add pure sc7 types/model/reply decoders and extend existing thin shared client with persistent multiplexed sockets, preserving one-shot exports. Test independently with real isolated socket server and bounded faults.

Add workbench-memory session owner and scope-aware client effects in extension; add trusted window-scoped privileged IDE lanes and mechanically synchronize reviewed pure core. Verify two-workbench/root isolation before enabling any temporary UI.
prerequisiteFlags: Private current contract/lifecycle fixtures pass; no shipped positive evidence

migrationSteps.action: Wire extension Settings/commands/webview and migrate IDE pane/actions/service/types/native Settings to v2-only manager path. Keep old IDs/legacy unrelated signatures. Add theme/keyboard UI, descriptors, dirty/reconciliation states and exact Delete/Discard.

Execute focused tests per task, then both-client native interaction, service/file/privacy/lifecycle evidence and final frozen builds/sweeps after implementation. Review manually per user direction, retain original failed/skipped results. Submit consumer proof without clearing external backend prerequisites.

Release manager mutations/temporary visibility only when genuine current S001/provider/worker-affinity/SQLServer and both-client evidence is independently accepted. Otherwise ship explicit upgrade/unsupported gate; never activate using fixture hashes or accepted historical test exceptions.

User-confirmed Saved changes/deletes are intentional data mutations and cannot be undone by rolling back UI. UI rollback first disables new mutation admission, preserves reconciliation/cleanup/end controls for live owners, cancels probes and drains/end sessions on workbench disposal. Never downgrade backend to binaries that discard receipt metadata or secret refs.

migration.backwardCompat: Backend wire contracts unchanged; IDE mirrored v2 declarations are additive, legacy arrays/results stay separate. Existing editor and action IDs preserved. Extension new aliases route same manager. Older daemon => explicit upgrade-required, no legacy upsert/remove fallback for manager. No registry migration, directory lookup redirection, persisted temporary form/session state or implicit family normalization.

alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One transport-free sc7 transition core, two host-specific renderers and lifecycle adapters.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Use a pure TypeScript state/projection core and strict v2 reply decoders shared by the extension and mechanically synchronized into the IDE fork with a pinned manifest. Extension reuses its injectable webview host conventions; IDE preserves DbDriversInput/pane and service/action identities. Each workbench owns a memory-only control connection independently of panel lifetime; scope-specific data and Saved lanes remain explicit. No new backend ownership or persistent client connection store.
pros: Smallest model that shares risky state/recovery semantics while respecting two existing host architectures
Core transcript fixtures and synchronized hashes detect client drift
cons: Two renderers require independent visual/keyboard evidence
Cross-repo sync and privileged IPC lifecycle must be tested
